title: Build SpecAugment and a Conformer block, then train a Conformer-CTC on digits
brief: Implement SpecAugment masking, Transformer-XL relative positions with the rel_shift trick, and a Conformer block module by module, then train a small Conformer-CTC on sequences of spoken digits and test it on a speaker it never heard.
hints: spec_augment: out = features.clone(), then slice-assign out[f0:f0 + f, :] and out[:, t0:t0 + t]. torch.randint's upper bound is exclusive, so draw from (low, high + 1) to include high.

relative_position_encoding: r = torch.arange(L - 1, -L, -1) gives the distances in row order. Build one (2L - 1, d / 2) table of r * w_i and write its sin into the even columns and its cos into the odd ones.

rel_shift has a pad-and-reshape trick: pad one zero column on the left to get (L, 2L), view it as (2L, L), drop the first row, view it as (L, 2L - 1), and keep the first L columns. Check it against x.gather with the index L - 1 - i + j.

In RelPositionMultiHeadAttention, add pos_bias_u and pos_bias_v to q while it is still (B, T, H, d_k), then transpose to (B, H, T, d_k). pos_emb projects to (2T - 1, H, d_k), which you transpose to (H, 2T - 1, d_k).
ConvolutionModule: mask with y.masked_fill(~mask[:, None, :], 0.0) after the GLU, when y is (B, d, T).
ConformerBlock: the two feed-forward modules each add half their output. The final LayerNorm is outside every residual.
